rows.grounds: points to the supreme Lord as locus
in the manner of a reflection

items.question: How does all this appear in the unchanging supreme Lord?
premises: All this shines forth in the unchanging supreme Lord.
It appears there in the manner of a reflection.
It does not appear as something external to him.
items.inference: The universe appears within the supreme Lord as reflection, not as an external reality.
items.plain_english: There, all this shines forth in the unchanging supreme Lord in the form of a reflection, and not as something external.

rows.grounds: in the space of pure awareness; sandhi before eva
cognitions of various bodies and so on
appearance of a snake and the like

items.question: Where and how do differentiated bodily cognitions appear to worldly beings?
premises: Such divided cognitions of various bodies appear to worldly beings.
They appear in the sky of consciousness, in Śiva alone.
This is like the appearance of a snake and so on in a rope.
items.inference: The differentiated world of embodied experience appears within consciousness alone, like a snake seen in a rope.
items.plain_english: In the sky of consciousness, in Śiva alone, such divided cognitions of various bodies appear to worldly beings, just as a snake and the like appear in a rope.

rows.grounds: the settled view prior to the death of the body
belongs to the domain of dream
after the death of the body
questions the nature of post-death embodiment

items.question: What kind of bodily existence can be established after death if prior embodiment is dreamlike?
premises: The established view before the death of the body belongs to the sphere of dream.
Another body and related experiences arise after death.
The nature of that post-death bodily arising is therefore questionable.
items.inference: If embodied life before death is dreamlike, the status of another body arising after death cannot be taken as independently real.
uncertainties: The verse is compressed and may be read as a rhetorical challenge rather than a direct assertion.
items.plain_english: Because the settled view before the body's death belongs to the realm of dream, what kind of other body or bodily arising after death could there really be?

rows.grounds: from the unfolding of mere appearance in general
by the power of that unfolding
are brought into being as separate realities

items.question: How do particular details arise in a dream without being independently produced?
premises: In a dream, particulars appear by the force of the unfolding of mere appearance.
Their manifestation comes from appearance itself, not from separate production.
Therefore those particulars are not produced as independent realities.
items.inference: Dream particulars are manifestations of appearance, not independently generated entities.
items.plain_english: In a dream, particular details appear by the force of the unfolding of mere appearance, but they are not produced as independent realities in that way.

rows.grounds: stones naturally marked with varied forms
containing diverse shapes within; sandhi before yathā
the inner delineations of the levels from māyā downward; sandhi before citaḥ
having a multiform core; sandhi before citaḥ

items.question: How can the varied levels of manifestation be contained within consciousness?
premises: Some śālagrāma stones naturally contain varied forms within themselves.
Consciousness has a variegated inner nature.
The inner delineations of the levels from māyā downward are contained within consciousness.
items.inference: The manifold levels of manifestation are inner differentiations within consciousness, not external additions to it.
items.plain_english: Just as some śālagrāma stones contain varied forms within them, so the inner delineations of the levels from māyā downward belong to the variegated heart of consciousness.

rows.grounds: worldly forms such as cities, oceans, and mountains; sandhi before tadicchā
conforming to the will of consciousness
having the nature of existent or nonexistent causes and effects

items.question: Do cities, oceans, mountains, and other forms act as independent causes or effects?
premises: Cities, oceans, mountains, and similar forms follow the will of consciousness.
They do not operate by themselves.
They do not independently possess the nature of existent or nonexistent causes and effects.
items.inference: The apparent causal structure of the world depends on the will of consciousness rather than on independent entities.
uncertainties: The compound sadasadrūpakāraṇākaraṇātmakāḥ is dense and allows slight variation in unpacking.
items.plain_english: Cities, oceans, mountains, and the like follow that will; they are not by themselves entities that independently function as existent or nonexistent causes and effects.

rows.grounds: when a rule has long taken root
in a fixed order or regulation
when no rule has yet taken root
this Lord; sandhi form of ayam
Bhairava as the space of consciousness

items.question: Does the Lord remain free both within established order and beyond it?
premises: A long-established rule may be cut off or set in motion.
Even where no rule has yet taken root, activity may arise.
In both cases the Lord remains independent.
items.inference: The consciousness-sky Bhairava is sovereign over both the maintenance and suspension of order.
items.plain_english: Whether by cutting off or setting in motion a long-established rule, or even where no rule has yet taken root, this Bhairava of the sky of consciousness remains independent.

rows.grounds: in the state sharing nondifference with Bhairava, full of only one consciousness
the reflective sense 'I am'; sandhi before anāmarśo
lack of reflective awareness; sandhi before bhedako
that which produces division; sandhi before bhāva
within the sphere of manifested entities

items.question: What causes differentiation within the realm of beings despite nondifference with Bhairava?
premises: The true state shares nondifference with Bhairava, full of one consciousness alone.
Within that state, the reflective awareness 'I am thus' may fail to occur.
That non-recognition differentiates the realm of beings.
items.inference: Differentiation arises from the absence of reflective recognition, not from any real division in consciousness.
items.plain_english: In that state which shares nondifference with Bhairava, full of one consciousness alone, the absence of the recognition 'I am thus' is what differentiates the realm of beings.

rows.grounds: by every valid means of knowing; sandhi before no
negates establishment; sandhi form before siddhaṃ
the emanation or projection of the world; sandhi before 'pi

items.question: Is any agent other than independent awareness established as the creator of manifestation?
premises: In a dream, no other agent is established by any means of knowledge.
Dream creation belongs to one's own awareness.
The world's creation should be understood in the same way as arising from independent self-awareness.
items.inference: Creation is the free activity of self-awareness, not the work of another agent.
items.plain_english: Just as no other agent is established in a dream by any means of knowledge, so too the creation should be understood as belonging to one's own independent awareness.

rows.grounds: in the mind's multiform city and garden
sporting or freely acting; sandhi before evaṃ
in the form of manifested entities; sandhi before bhūtaiś
as those that have come to be; sandhi before cinmātrakair
consisting of consciousness alone; sandhi before iti

items.question: What recognition arises for one who plays within the mind's variegated display?
premises: One may sport within the mind's variegated city and garden of appearances.
Such a one can recognize the true identity behind those appearances.
The recognition is that 'I alone abide as all these beings, which are consciousness only.'
items.inference: True recognition sees all manifested beings as the self's own consciousness-only forms.
items.plain_english: One who plays in the mind's variegated city and garden knows: 'I alone abide as all these beings that have come to be, and they are nothing but consciousness.'

the reflective sense 'I am'; sandhi form of asmi+iti
the diverse experiences of birth and death
in that which has no birth
in that which does not die
on the screen or surface of the mind

items.question: Where do the varied experiences of birth and death actually appear?
premises: The sense 'I am born' and 'I am dead' arises as a reflective appearance.
The diverse forms of birth and death appear in the unborn and deathless reality.
They appear on the wall of the mind as self-imagined projections.
items.inference: Birth and death are imagined appearances within the unborn, deathless consciousness.
items.plain_english: The varied experiences of 'I am born' and 'I am dead' appear in the unborn and deathless, on the wall of the mind, as projections of one's own imagination.

rows.grounds: the status of being another world or this world
even when time, division, awareness, and place are not truly divided; sandhi before 'py
emphasizes the concession; sandhi form of api

items.question: Are this world and the other world truly different realities?
premises: The distinction between this world and the other world is only a matter of awareness.
Even apparent divisions of time, part, awareness, and place do not create real difference.
The underlying reality remains non-differentiated.
items.inference: World-distinctions are modes of awareness within an undivided reality.
uncertainties: The compound akālakalāsaṃviddeśabhede is compact and its internal relations are interpretively dense.
items.plain_english: Being this world or another world is only a matter of awareness; even amid apparent divisions of time, part, awareness, and place, it remains undivided.

rows.grounds: the manifested world; sandhi before mūrtaś
having concrete form; sandhi before cen
by anyone at all; sandhi of kena+ekaḥ
a mountain, as example of a material object

items.question: Could any material object be perceived if creation were not consciousness-made?
premises: Suppose this creation were merely material and not made of consciousness.
Perception would then have to arise from within that material creation.
No one could perceive even a single mountain from within such a merely material creation.
items.inference: Because perception occurs, creation cannot be merely material; it must be consciousness-made.
items.plain_english: If this creation were merely material and not made of consciousness, then no one could perceive even a single mountain from within it.

rows.grounds: of the class of elements, subtle elements, and so on; sandhi before ādhāra
in examining what supports and what is supported
identical with Śiva's own nature; sandhi of śivarūpā+eva

items.question: What ultimately supports the elements and subtle elements in their mutual dependence?
premises: The elements, subtle elements, and related classes can be examined as support and supported.
Such examination cannot rest in another material support without regress.
Ultimately the supporting principle is the consciousness-power that is Śiva's own nature.
items.inference: The final support of all dependent manifestation is Śiva's consciousness-power.
items.plain_english: When one examines the elements, subtle elements, and the rest in terms of support and what is supported, in the end it is the consciousness-power, identical with Śiva's own nature, that upholds them.

rows.grounds: emphasizes this very mode; sandhi of eva+ittham

items.question: Why is cognition identified as the creative agent and called the common ground?
premises: Cognition itself is the creative agent in this mode of manifestation.
That cognition is manifestation and is Śiva in his own self.
Because it is the shared basis of manifestation, it is called the common power.
items.inference: Creative cognition is Śiva's own power and the common ground of all manifestation.
uncertainties: The exact nuance of sādhārasaṃjñitā may be 'called common' or 'called the common basis'.
items.plain_english: Therefore cognition itself is the agent; that manifestation is Śiva in his own self. For that reason, this power is called the common ground.

rows.grounds: in the power that is its own support
due to repose; sandhi before viśvam

items.question: Why does even an apparently unsupported imagined appearance not collapse?
premises: An imagined appearance may seem to have no support.
Yet it does not fall away into collapse.
This is because the universe rests in its own supporting power.
items.inference: All appearances, even imagined ones, are upheld by the self-supporting power of consciousness.
items.plain_english: Even what is imagined and seems without support does not fall away, because the universe rests in its own supporting power; reflect on it in this way.

from the fixation expressed as 'I' and so on; sandhi before eva
the condition of earth and the lower levels
the recognition 'I am consciousness'; sandhi of cit+asmi+iti

items.question: How does the dense sense of ego give rise to the levels of manifestation and culminate in Bhairava identity?
premises: From the fixation of the dense sense 'I' arise the states beginning with earth.
This same process extends through the levels of manifestation.
At its culmination, the recognition 'I am consciousness' is realized as Bhairava identity.
items.inference: The spectrum from gross egoity to earth and back to pure recognition culminates in the realization of Bhairava identity.
items.plain_english: From the fixation of the dense 'I' and so on arises the state beginning with earth, until at last the recognition 'I am consciousness' is fulfilled as the identity of Bhairava.

rows.grounds: in a gem; sandhi before indrāyudhe
in radiance or appearance; sandhi before iva
from the highest standpoint; sandhi before eṣāṃ
no real connection with arising and passing away

items.question: Do the varied appearances in Śiva truly arise and pass away?
premises: Colors like blue appear in a jewel or rainbow as expressions of light.
So too varied appearances manifest in Śiva.
In ultimate truth, these appearances have no real arising or dissolution.
items.inference: Appearances in Śiva are like colors in light: manifest without ultimate origination or destruction.
items.plain_english: Like blue and other colors in a jewel or in a rainbow's light, so appearances are in Śiva; but in ultimate truth they have no real arising or passing away.

of direction and time; sandhi before api
extends the claim to space and time themselves

items.question: Can creation be properly located within space and time?
premises: It is incoherent to say that creation occurs in space or in time.
The Lord whose nature is consciousness is the creator.
Space and time themselves are part of that creation.
items.inference: Creation cannot be placed within space and time, because space and time arise from the conscious Lord's creative act.
items.plain_english: To say that creation happens in space or in time is incoherent, for the creation of the conscious Lord includes space and time as well.

rows.grounds: in what is taken to be the waking state
within the range of three and a half cubits
within a single watch of the day
distinct dream worlds; sandhi before citra
having their own varied measures of space and time

items.question: How do dreams reveal the relativity of space and time within waking assumptions?
premises: What is assumed to be waking occurs within limited space and a limited watch of time.
Within that same span, separate dreams can occur.
Those dreams have their own varied measures of space and time.
items.inference: The measures of space and time are not fixed by waking assumptions, since distinct dream worlds generate their own.
items.plain_english: Within what is taken as waking, in a span of three and a half cubits and a single watch of time, separate dreams arise with their own varied measures of space and time.

rows.grounds: any definite thing; sandhi before api
in a moment of action; sandhi before 'pi

items.question: Is a moment a fixed unit of time if many actions occur within it?
premises: A so-called moment is not regarded as any fixed thing.
Even within a single moment of action, many swift actions can occur.
Therefore the moment cannot be an ultimate, indivisible unit.
items.inference: The moment is not an absolute temporal atom but a relative measure within experience.
items.plain_english: Therefore we do not regard a moment as anything fixed, for even within a single moment of action there are many swift actions.

rows.grounds: by a narrow channel, metaphor for constricted view
those who depend on a doctrine of emptiness

items.question: What is the limitation of those who reduce manifestation to momentary contraction?
premises: Some accept that the contraction of beings ends in a moment.
This view narrows reality to a constricted channel.
Such thinkers rely on an emptiness-based outlook.
items.inference: Reducing manifestation to momentary contraction reflects a constricted, emptiness-leaning perspective rather than the full view of consciousness.
uncertainties: The metaphor nālyā is somewhat interpretive; it suggests a narrow tube or channel.
items.plain_english: Therefore those who hold that the contraction of beings ends in a moment surely rely, through this narrow channel, on a view grounded in emptiness.

rows.grounds: the one who; sandhi before eva
of what exists; sandhi before bhāvāñ

the sovereign one; sandhi before sa

items.question: Who has the sovereign power to make the existent appear empty and the nonexistent appear manifest?
premises: The same sovereign power can reduce existent beings to emptiness.
That same power can make what is nonexistent appear clearly.
This capacity belongs to the Lord because of his independence.
items.inference: The supreme Lord's freedom alone accounts for the appearance of existence and nonexistence.
uncertainties: The token tahtāsataḥ is unusual in form; taken here as tathā+asataḥ in sense.
items.plain_english: Therefore the one who, by his independence, is able to make existent beings appear empty and likewise make the nonexistent appear clearly is the supreme Lord.

rows.grounds: the highest sovereign; sandhi before viśvarūpaḥ
having the universe as his form
of anything at all; sandhi of kasya+api
of earth and the other levels; sandhi before upapannatā
the state of being established as independent

items.question: Is the universe-form a property of the supreme Lord or of any separate entity like earth?
premises: The supreme Lord is proclaimed in this way as having the universe as his form.
No separate entity such as earth and the rest is independently tenable as the basis of that form.
Therefore universe-form belongs to the supreme Lord alone.
items.inference: The universe is the form of the supreme Lord, not of any independently real separate entity.
items.plain_english: Thus the supreme Lord is proclaimed as having the universe as his form; no separate entity such as earth or the rest can be established as independently real in that way.
